titleEn: How to File a Renovation Insurance Claim in British Columbia
titleZh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省装修保险理赔完整流程指南
contentEn:
When damage hits your BC home, knowing how your insurance works means the difference between a smooth payout and a months-long dispute with your insurer. In BC, home renovation insurance claims are governed by the Insurance Act and reviewed by the Financial Institutions Regulatory Authority (BCFIRA). Reno Stars has helped dozens of Greater Vancouver homeowners document damage, complete the claim forms correctly, and get their restorations underway without delay.

The BC Insurance Act sets a hard 12-month deadline from the date of loss to file your claim. If you miss that window, your insurer can legally deny payment regardless of how valid your claim is. Document everything immediately, because the insurer's adjuster will ask for receipts, photos, and contractor estimates before authorizing any payout.

What does a standard BC home renovation insurance policy actually cover?

BC home insurance policies typically cover damage caused by fire, smoke, water escaping from pipes or appliances, windstorms, and falling objects. They do not cover damage from gradual leaks that went unreported, rot that resulted from deferred maintenance, or renovations done without the proper permits. The difference matters: a burst poly-B pipe that soaked your kitchen floor overnight is a covered peril; the slow drip under your sink that caused mold over six months is typically excluded as maintenance failure.

Your policy also carries a deductible — the amount you pay before coverage kicks in. Most BC homeowners carry a $1,000 deductible, though higher deductibles lower your premium. If your claim is for $22,000 in water damage and your deductible is $1,000, the insurer sends $21,000 if the claim is approved.

Does insurance pay for a full kitchen or bathroom renovation in BC?

Insurance covers the cost to restore your home to its pre-loss condition, not to upgrade it. If your ten-year-old kitchen was destroyed by a covered peril, the insurer pays depreciated value or replacement cost for materials of similar quality — not the premium finishes you might have chosen if you were renovating by choice. You can upgrade at your own expense, but the insurance payout is based on standard-grade materials and labour in your area.

For a partial kitchen loss — a single cabinet run or countertop — the insurer typically hires its own contractor to provide an estimate. Getting an independent contractor's quote from a company like Reno Stars and submitting it alongside the adjuster's report often leads to a more accurate settlement.

How long does a home renovation insurance claim take in BC?

Simple claims with clear documentation can close in four to six weeks. Complicated claims involving structural damage, contested liability, or multiple contractors can take three to six months. BCFIRA reports that disputed claims — where the insurer and homeowner disagree on scope or cost — make up roughly 18% of closed files and take significantly longer to resolve.

If the insurer's offer seems too low, you have the right to request an appraisal under the Insurance Act. Two appraisers (one chosen by each party) determine the fair replacement value. Reno Stars can provide detailed, line-item estimates that support your position in that process.

What if your claim is denied or underpaid?

BC homeowners have three avenues if an insurer refuses or underpays: request an appraisal under the Insurance Act, file a complaint with BCFIRA, or pursue mediation. Each has costs and timelines. Document every communication with your insurer from day one — written records of phone calls and emails are essential if a dispute escalates.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long do I have to file a home insurance claim in BC?

You have 12 months from the date of loss under the BC Insurance Act. Filing sooner is strongly recommended, as delays make documentation harder and increase the risk the insurer questions the cause of damage.

Does BC home insurance cover renovation work done without permits?

No. Work completed without required permits is a policy exclusion. Always pull your permits before starting any renovation in Greater Vancouver.

Will insurance pay for a full kitchen renovation if damage is partial?

Insurance covers only the scope of actual damage, not a full room renovation. If a burst pipe destroyed your lower cabinets but your upper cabinets were undamaged, the insurer covers replacement of the lower run only.

Can I hire my own contractor instead of the insurer's preferred vendor?

Yes. BC homeowners are not required to use the insurer's suggested contractor. You can hire anyone licensed in BC, including Reno Stars, and submit the contractor's estimate as part of your claim documentation.

BC省住宅保险理赔流程与 homeowner熟悉索赔规则密切相关。BC省《保险法》规定了严格的12个月索赔时效，从损失发生之日起算。Reno Stars帮助大温哥华地区的房主完成保险理赔表格、记录损失，并顺利启动修复施工。

BC省《保险法》明确规定被保险人有责任在合理时间内修复损失部位。保险覆盖火灾、烟雾、水管或电器漏水、风灾和坠落物造成的损坏。不涵盖的范围包括：未及时报告的渐进性渗漏、长期维护不当导致的腐烂，以及无许可证装修工程。

BC住宅装修保险通常涵盖哪些范围？

BC省标准家庭保险政策通常涵盖火灾、烟雾、水管或电器漏水、风灾和坠落物造成的损坏。不涵盖的范围包括：未及时报告的渐进性渗漏、长期维护不当导致的腐烂，以及无许可证装修工程。《保险法》明确指出，被保险人有责任在合理时间内修复损坏部位。

大多数BC房主的基本免赔额为1,000加元。如果理赔金额为22,000加元，免赔额为1,000加元，则保险公司赔付21,000加元。

保险是否支付完整厨房或浴室装修费用？

保险仅覆盖恢复至损失前状态的费用，而非升级改造。若十年前的厨房因管道爆裂全损，保险公司按当时同类标准材料折旧值赔偿，房主若想升级需自费。Reno Stars可提供详细的分项估算，为理赔过程提供专业支持。

BC省家庭装修保险理赔需要多长时间？

文件齐全的简单理赔可在四至六周内结案。涉及结构损坏、责任争议或多位承包商的复杂理赔可能需要三至六个月。BCFIRA数据显示，约18%的已结理赔案件涉及争议，平均处理时间显著更长。

如果保险公司的报价过低，投保人有权依据《保险法》申请评估鉴定，向BCFIRA提交投诉或进行调解。从第一天起保存所有书面沟通记录至关重要。Reno Stars可提供详细的逐项估算，支持理赔争议中的专业立场。

如果理赔被拒绝或赔付金额不足怎么办？

BC省房主有权依据《保险法》申请评估鉴定、向BCFIRA提交投诉或进行调解。每种途径都有成本和时间线。从第一天起保存所有书面沟通记录至关重要。Reno Stars可提供详细的逐项估算，支持理赔争议中的专业立场。

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

常见问题

BC省装修保险理赔的时效是多久？

根据BC省《保险法》，从损失发生之日起，您有12个月的时间提交保险理赔。越早提交越好，因为延迟会增加举证难度。

无许可证的装修工程保险是否覆盖？

不覆盖。无许可证装修工程是保险除外责任。在大温哥华地区进行任何装修工程前，务必申请所需许可证。

部分损坏时保险是否支付完整厨房装修？

保险仅覆盖实际损坏范围。若爆裂管道仅损坏了下柜，上柜完好，保险公司只赔付下柜更换费用。

业主是否可以聘请自己的承包商而非保险公司指定的供应商？

可以。BC省房主有权选择任何持牌承包商，包括Reno Stars，并提交其估算报告作为理赔文件的一部分。
